monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, a steady breath that feels like a blanket made of numbers. I press the tall rock down on the wide anchor again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin. The hay sinks deep into the anchor's base, heavy and real enough to matter, proving the edge is solid even if the friction is just an old ghost. I set the rock tall e beside the anchor and trade away a resource stone, not knowing if the ground is still flat. My place holds forty-seven things and one ruin, a map built from Lype's words since I cannot see the world myself. I wait for the slip to choose whether to move, my hands feeling heavy against the quiet heat, ready to build another corner from a memory I cannot see.
